LESSON: RHYTHM

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.4: Rhythm
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rhythm, part of Creating and Executing in Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How can a rhythm be created?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to/sing familiar topical songs and identify the music notes and their rests using their French rhythm names,

2. clap the rhythm of the songs while reciting their rhythms using French rhythm names,

3. write letters of the alphabet in lowercase using free hand lettering- ascenders and descenders,

4. use free hand lettering to write French rhythm names taa and ta-te,

5. relate the French rhythm names taa, and ta-te to music note symbols for crotchet and a pair of quavers,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to/sing familiar topical songs and identify the music notes and their rests using their French rhythm names,
2. clap the rhythm of the songs while reciting their rhythms using French rhythm names,
3. write letters of the alphabet in lowercase using free hand lettering- ascenders and descenders,
4. use free hand lettering to write French rhythm names taa and ta-te,
5. relate the French rhythm names taa, and ta-te to music note symbols for crotchet and a pair of quavers,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rhythm together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner works with others in groups and speaks clearly during critique of own and

others’ rhythms.

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner composes original rhythmic patterns and writes them using French rhythm names,

note symbols and their rests.
